A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MASt3R-SLAM work. Their complete main texts and supplementary material are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory estimation, dense reconstruction, component ablation and runtime results, including supplementary evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds a loop-closure ablation measuring trajectory and reconstruction accuracy.

M1.justification: The MASt3R prior, projective matching, feature refinement, Sim(3) tracking, pointmap fusion, loop closure and backend optimisation are unchanged. The new appendix explains existing components, and disabling loop closure is an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TUM RGB-D, 7-Scenes, ETH3D-SLAM and EuRoC, and retain the Burghers and changing-zoom demonstrations. The new ablation uses existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding trajectory, reconstruction and matching comparisons retain their comparator sets. Renamed matching variants match existing rows, while the added MASt3R-SfM discussion does not introduce a new evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New Table 7 introduces a with/without-loop-closure control in calibrated and uncalibrated modes, including ATE on the EuRoC Vicon subset. Existing sampling, alignment, metrics, preprocessing and supplementary evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted loop-closure ablation covering trajectory accuracy on TUM, 7-Scenes and EuRoC Vicon, plus reconstruction accuracy on EuRoC Vicon. The existing matching, fusion and point-versus-ray analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Across-sequence averages and RMSE reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises 7-Scenes accuracy/completion/Chamfer from 0.141/0.048/0.094 to 0.115/0.040/0.077 for DROID-SLAM, and from 0.089/0.085/0.087 to 0.074/0.057/0.066 for calibrated Ours. Table 7 adds loop-closure results, including calibrated EuRoC Vicon ATE of 0.233 without versus 0.029 with loop closure. Existing trajectory and runtime results are retained.

T1.justification: The central-camera assumptions, Sim(3) formulation and supplementary Jacobian derivations are unchanged. v1's displayed standard Levenberg-Marquardt update is replaced by a prose reference to the same solver, without revising mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about real-time SLAM using two-view reconstruction priors, generic time-varying cameras, consistent dense geometry and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: v2 revises the fusion explanation to associate recent pointmaps with drift and first pointmaps with insufficient baseline. It interprets loop-closure gains as evidence of prediction bias and drift, and adds discussion of low-parallax geometry and changing-intrinsics limitations of competing systems. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the front-page project and video links. Hardware, input resolution, CUDA implementation information, initialization, thresholds and runtime details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Hagemann et al.'s camera self-calibration work. New supplementary Section 13 expands comparisons with DROID/DPV-SLAM and MASt3R-SfM concerning geometry coherence, camera assumptions, matching and optimisation, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several passages, renames and reorders Ablation Studies as Component Analysis, adds an acknowledgement and supplementary comparison section, and shortens the solver explanation. The overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, rearranges and compresses the existing ablation tables, introduces a paired point/ray display, and moves Table 2 from PDF page 7 to page 6. Tables and figures are reflowed, while the original figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new loop-closure control supplies useful evidence for the system's global consistency, while revised fusion explanations and supplementary comparisons improve clarity. These are modest gains within an already evaluated system. Removal of access links and unexplained revisions to Table 3's scores are drawbacks that limit the overall improvement.
